newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors grill former defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors grill former defence minister.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors grilled sacked defence minister Lee Yang-ho for more than 12 hours over allegations he took bribes in an arms deal, prosecution officials said on Friday.
"After Mr Lee was summoned last night, the investigation continued throughout the night and he is still being questioned," one official told Reuters.
"No concrete steps have been taken yet. Mr Lee and three Daewoo officials are still under investigation."

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics has charged that Lee and a Korean-American arms dealer split a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Daewoo said it gave money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe.
Lee has not commented publicly on the charges, but state media have quoted him as denying any wrongdoing.

President Kim Young-sam removed Lee from his post on October 17 as part of a reshuffle of the military's top brass. The reshuffle followed harsh criticism of the military for failing to prevent an incursion by a North Korean submarine last month.
Hours after Lee's dismissal, the National Congress for New Politics accused Lee of taking the bribes. President Kim has ordered a full investigation.
Investigators are also questioning Sok Chin-chol, one-time president of Daewoo Heavy, Yoon Young-suk, chairman of Daewoo Group, and Chung Ho-shin, vice president of Daewoo Heavy.

Another prosecution official said Lee's wife, Kim Hye-sook, told investigators on Thursday she gave a diamond ring and diamond necklace to former president Roh Tae-woo's daughter shortly before Lee was promoted to air force chief of staff.

Roh's daughter, So-young, told prosecutors on Wednesday she received the jewellery through the arms dealer's wife but returned it after learning that it was given to solicit a favour, prosecutors said.
The arms dealer, Kwon Pyong-ho, had earlier told South Korean reporters in Beijing the jewels were given to try to secure Lee's promotion. Kwon's remarks were broadcast in South Korea.
Lee headed the air force during Roh's presidency. He became defence minister after Kim was elected president in 1993.
The affair has embarrassed the president, who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption crusade that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being found guilty in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both are appealing.
Daewoo Group founder Kim Woo-choong is appealing a two-year jail sentence imposed for bribing Roh. He was one of nine businessmen convicted on similar charges.
